newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIEST TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIEST TRADE.

text.p: HARARE, July 3 (Reutetr) - Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely stable in quiet trade on Thursday, dealers said.

They said the market opened with a Z$60 million surplus but, with no maturities expected during the day, the central Reserve Bank opted not to have its usual daily treasury bill auction to mop up liquidity.
The central bank bills were however being sold on the secondary market at a steady 24.75 percent while call money eased to 22 percent from 23.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought steadily at 26.5 percent and sold at 25 and bankers acceptance bills were also quoted unchanged at 25.5 percent (buying) but were softer at 24.75 from 25 on the sell-side.
